no: Let L_{A} be the orthic axis of triangle BCX(4), and define L_{B}, L_{C} cyclically. Let A' = L_{B} ∩ L_{C}, B' = L_{C} ∩ L_{A}, C' = L_{A} ∩ L_{B}. Triangle A'B'C' is here named the **orthic axes triangle**. A'B'C' is also the cevian triangle of X_4 wrt the orthic triangle. A'B'C' is perspective to ABC at X_4, and homothetic to the polar triangle of the nine-point circle at X_427. The orthic axes of ABC, the orthic triangle, and the orthic axes triangle concur in X_2501. (Randy Hutson, August 19, 2019)
